mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2% YoY signals inflationary pressures that typically lead to monetary tightening, which in turn increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If CPIAUCSL YoY > 2% and S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of the triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in one month signals a weakening labor market, which typically precedes a broader economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If UNRATE rises > 0.5% in 1 month and S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of the triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real GDP (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters signals a strengthening economy, which boosts corporate earnings and consumer confidence, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If GDPC1 increases over two consecutive quarters and S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are negative in more than 40% of the periods.

mechanism_narrative: A significant decline in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% in one month signals a supply-side contraction, which can lead to reduced corporate earnings and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If INDPRO declines > 2% in 1 month and S&P 500 forward 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of the triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) increase by more than 5% month-over-month, it signals a strengthening housing market, which typically boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If HOUST increases > 5% MoM and S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are negative in more than 40% of the triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 jobs in a month, it signals a strong labor market, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If PAYEMS increases > 200,000 jobs in 1 month and S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are negative in more than 40% of the triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 1% and the real GDP (GDPC1) is contracting, it signals a liquidity trap, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days due to economic stagnation.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS < 1% and GDPC1 is contracting, but S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of the triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: When retail sales (RSAFS) decline by more than 2% month-over-month and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) rises by more than 0.3% in the same month, it signals a weakening consumer demand environment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS declines > 2% MoM and UNRATE rises > 0.3% in 1 month
failure_condition: If RSAFS declines > 2% MoM and UNRATE rises > 0.3% in 1 month, but S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of the triggered instances.
